title: How a Massachusetts Board Disciplinary Matter Runs, and What It Puts on the Clock
topic: Licensure and discipline / Board disciplinary procedure, sanctions and deadlines
subtopic: The route from complaint to disposition under 247 CMR 10.02, 10.04 and 10.05, the actions available to the Board under 247 CMR 10.06, pre-hearing summary action under 247 CMR 10.07 and 10.08, the licensee reporting periods in 247 CMR 10.03(1)(y), (z) and (aa), and reinstatement after suspension or revocation under 247 CMR 4.02(6) and (7)
learning_objectives: Trace a matter from the communication that becomes a complaint through the Board's choice of track to a disposition under 247 CMR 10.06.
State what makes a communication a complaint within the meaning of 247 CMR 10.02, and when in the process that happens.
Distinguish an investigative conference from an adjudicatory hearing, and say whether the Board must hold either one before the other.
Sort the actions listed in 247 CMR 10.06 into those that constitute formal disciplinary action and those that do not.
Separate the seven-day hearing clock in 247 CMR 10.07 from the 15-business-day hearing clock in 247 CMR 10.08(3), and say what each one is measured from.
Say which periods in this area are owed by the Board and which are owed by the registrant or licensee.
Apply the seven-business-day and 30-day reporting periods in 247 CMR 10.03(1)(y), (z) and (aa) to a set of facts.
State what a voluntary surrender agreement must say, and what the registrant gives up by signing it.
Place a suspended or revoked registration in the correct reinstatement tier under 247 CMR 4.02(6) or (7) and name what changes between them.

orientation.text: A Massachusetts disciplinary matter has a defined beginning, a Board choice in the middle, and a small set of possible endings, and 247 CMR 10.00 supplies all three. It begins with a complaint, and 247 CMR 10.02 defines that word narrowly: a complaint is a communication filed with the Board or the Division of Health Professions Licensure which the Board determines, after investigation, merits further consideration or action. The Board's determination is therefore part of the definition rather than something that happens to a complaint later. A letter of grievance is a communication on the day it arrives; it becomes a complaint when the Board, having investigated, decides it merits further consideration or action. 247 CMR 10.05 then gives the Board its choice: after receipt of a complaint and all related investigative materials the Board may schedule an investigative conference, or may schedule a formal adjudicatory hearing pursuant to M.G.L. c. 30A and 801 CMR 1.01 if it determines that one is required.

The two tracks differ in formality and in the document that opens them. An investigative conference is defined at 247 CMR 10.02 as an informal discussion relating to a complaint held with the Board, and under 247 CMR 10.04 the Board may schedule one at any time prior to the commencement of a formal adjudicatory proceeding, giving timely notice which shall include a general statement of the nature of the issues to be discussed. An adjudicatory hearing is a formal administrative hearing held by the Board to determine the truth and validity of complaints filed against a registrant or licensee, conducted pursuant to M.G.L. c. 30A and 801 CMR 1.01. The instrument that summons a registrant to it is the Order to Show Cause, which 247 CMR 10.02 defines as a document served by the Board upon a registrant ordering the registrant or licensee to appear before the Board for a formal adjudicatory hearing. Because 247 CMR 10.04 makes the conference available at any time before a formal proceeding commences and 247 CMR 10.05 offers the two as alternatives, the informal conference is an option the Board holds and not a gateway the Board has to pass through.

What the Board may do at the end is a list in 247 CMR 10.06, and the list is only loosely a ladder, because its first two items are not discipline at all. Dismissal of the complaint comes first. The second is the advisory letter, an official written document retained in the Board's files delineating the Board's concerns with the registrant's or licensee's professional practice, and the regulation states in terms that an advisory letter does not constitute formal disciplinary action. The sanctions are items (3) through (5). A reprimand constitutes formal disciplinary action, and a censure is a severe reprimand, so a censure is the heavier of the pair rather than a separate lesser category; what 247 CMR 10.06(3) does not do is attach any suspension or restriction of practice to either of them. Probation constitutes disciplinary action and consists of a period of time during which the registrant or licensee may practise under conditions imposed by the Board pursuant to a formal adjudicatory hearing or consent agreement, which makes it the sanction defined as practice under Board conditions rather than the only one that leaves the registrant working. Suspension or revocation of a personal registration, pharmacy permit, licence or controlled substance registration may be imposed pursuant to a decision and order of the Board following a formal adjudicatory hearing or following the execution of a consent agreement. The list continues past item (5), and what 247 CMR 10.06(8) and (9) supply are notices imposing what 247 CMR 10.08(1) calls non-disciplinary cessation or restriction; what may be disciplined, and whose credentials the Board reaches, belongs to the companion section on grounds and is not taught here.

Not every restriction waits for the end of the process, and the two instruments that do not wait are easy to confuse because both answer an immediate or serious threat. 247 CMR 10.07 permits the Board, where it determines on affidavits or other documentary evidence that a licensee is an immediate or serious threat to the public health, safety or welfare, to suspend or refuse to renew a licence pending a final hearing on the merits of the allegations, and it fixes the price of acting that early: a hearing limited to the determination of the necessity of the summary action shall be afforded the licensee within seven days of the Board's action. 247 CMR 10.08 supplies a second and different instrument. Where the Board or Board President determines on affidavits or other evidence that a registrant or licensee, or the products prepared by a registrant or licensee, are an immediate or serious threat, a Cease and Desist Notice or Quarantine Notice may issue, and what such a notice imposes is expressly a non-disciplinary cessation or restriction of pharmacy operations, or a non-disciplinary restriction on the registrant or licensee to the extent necessary to avert a continued threat pending final investigation results. The hearing clock attached to a notice is 15 business days, not seven days, and under 247 CMR 10.08(2) the requirements of the notice remain in effect until the Board or Board President rescinds or amends them, or until the Board takes final action on any related pending complaint and issues a final decision.

The deadlines that fall on the licensee rather than on the Board sit in a different part of the regulation and are not hearing clocks at all. They appear in 247 CMR 10.03(1), which is the list of grounds for discipline, so missing one of them is itself something the Board may discipline for. Under 247 CMR 10.03(1)(y) it is a ground for discipline to fail to report, or to fail to report accurately, to the Board within seven business days, in a manner and format determined by the Board, discipline under 247 CMR 10.06 on the basis of actions listed in 247 CMR 10.03(1). Under 247 CMR 10.03(1)(z) the same seven business days runs on any final action, including licence surrender or resignation, regarding a registrant or licensee by any other governmental authority in this state or another jurisdiction, and the subsection expressly reaches action against any other health care related professional registration or licence the person holds, so an out-of-state sanction on a nursing or medical credential is caught by it. Under 247 CMR 10.03(1)(aa) a pending criminal charge or conviction, in Massachusetts or any other jurisdiction, is reported to the Board in writing within 30 days. Seven days and seven business days are not the same period: of those two, the one measured in business days is the licensee's and the one measured in plain days is the Board's. The unit alone does not settle whose clock it is, because the 30-day period in 247 CMR 10.03(1)(aa) is the licensee's and is measured in plain days too.

A matter can end without an adjudicatory hearing in more than one way: 247 CMR 10.06(1) and (2) let the Board dismiss the complaint or issue an advisory letter without holding either track, and 247 CMR 10.06(6) supplies the negotiated ending. A consent agreement is a resolution of a complaint agreed upon by the Board and the registrant or licensee which may contain conditions placed by the Board on the registrant's or licensee's professional conduct and practice, and which may include the voluntary suspension or surrender of a personal registration, pharmacy permit, licence or controlled substance registration. The next sentence says of the voluntary surrender alone that it may be permanent or for a fixed period of time, so that phrase belongs to the surrender and not to the voluntary suspension named beside it. Surrender inside such an agreement is not an informal exit from a difficult file. The voluntary surrender agreement shall be in writing and be signed by the registrant or licensee and the Board; shall recite the facts upon which it is based and include, but not be limited to, provisions addressing reinstatement and any conditions the Board may elect to impose; shall state that the registrant or licensee realises that the surrender is an act which deprives him or her of all privileges of registration and is not subject to judicial review; and shall be placed in the registrant's or licensee's Board file as part of the permanent Board records. The consent agreement is also one of the two routes by which probation, suspension and revocation may be imposed under 247 CMR 10.06(4) and (5), the other being a formal adjudicatory hearing, so the negotiated ending and the adjudicated ending can arrive at the same sanction by different paths.

The last period in this area runs after the sanction rather than during the process. 247 CMR 4.02(6) provides that an applicant for personal registration renewal whose personal registration has been revoked or has been suspended for between six months and two years shall take and pass the Multistate Pharmacy Jurisprudence Examination and meet all conditions as determined by the Board as a prerequisite to registration renewal. 247 CMR 4.02(7) provides that an applicant whose personal registration has been revoked or suspended for more than two years shall take and pass the MPJE and meet all other conditions as determined by the Board, which may include taking and passing the NAPLEX, as a prerequisite to registration renewal. The MPJE is therefore common to both tiers and settles nothing between them; the NAPLEX is named only in the longer tier, and even there it is named as something the Board's conditions may include rather than as an automatic requirement. The bands are not symmetrical, and the words show why. 247 CMR 4.02(6) says has been revoked or has been suspended for between six months and two years, repeating has been, so the six-months-to-two-years band belongs to the suspension limb and a revocation sits inside 4.02(6) with no band attached to it. 247 CMR 4.02(7) says has been revoked or suspended for more than two years, with the period governing both limbs, so a revocation that has stood for more than two years is inside 4.02(7) as well. For a revocation, then, the MPJE requirement holds either way, and what the longer period changes is that the Board's other conditions may include the NAPLEX. Two boundaries are worth fixing. This is the ladder for a registration that was suspended or revoked, and a registration that merely lapsed without ever being suspended or revoked returns by a different route which this section does not teach. And neither subsection states a requirement for a suspension shorter than six months, so nothing here should be applied to one.

worked_examples.scenario: A pharmacist receives written notice that the Board has scheduled an investigative conference about a complaint concerning her dispensing records. The notice contains a general statement of the nature of the issues to be discussed. Her employer's counsel tells her that the conference is the first mandatory step of a hearing sequence, that a formal adjudicatory hearing can only follow it, and that the notice is effectively an Order to Show Cause. She asks what the conference actually is and what it is not.
steps: Start with what the regulation calls it. 247 CMR 10.02 defines an investigative conference as an informal discussion relating to a complaint held with the Board, which is a different thing from the formal administrative hearing that 247 CMR 10.02 defines as an adjudicatory hearing.

Check when it may be scheduled. Under 247 CMR 10.04 the Board may schedule an investigative conference at any time prior to the commencement of a formal adjudicatory proceeding, and shall give timely notice including a general statement of the nature of the issues to be discussed, which is what she has received.

Check whether it is mandatory. 247 CMR 10.05 provides that after receipt of a complaint and all related investigative materials the Board may schedule an investigative conference or may schedule a formal adjudicatory hearing, so the two are alternatives and the conference is not a prerequisite.

Identify the document that does open the formal track. An Order to Show Cause is defined at 247 CMR 10.02 as a document served by the Board upon a registrant ordering the registrant or licensee to appear before the Board for a formal adjudicatory hearing, which this notice is not.

Note what has already happened before either track opens. Her file became a complaint within the meaning of 247 CMR 10.02 only when the Board determined, after investigation, that the communication merited further consideration or action.
worked_examples.resolution: The conference is an informal discussion the Board has elected to hold, it is not a required gateway to a formal hearing, and the notice is not an Order to Show Cause. The error the scenario invites is treating the stages of 247 CMR 10.00 as a fixed sequence every matter must climb, when 247 CMR 10.05 gives the Board a choice between the informal and the formal track after investigation.

worked_examples.scenario: A Massachusetts pharmacist also holds a nursing licence in a neighbouring state. On a Monday that state's nursing board enters a final action against the nursing licence. Eleven days later she is criminally charged in Massachusetts with an offence unrelated to her practice. She decides to wait until the criminal case is resolved and then report both matters together, on the view that the nursing action is not a pharmacy matter and that an unproved charge is nothing to report.
steps: Locate the duties. Both sit in 247 CMR 10.03(1), the list of grounds for discipline, so a failure to report is itself a ground on which the Board may discipline her.

Take the out-of-state action first. 247 CMR 10.03(1)(z) requires report to the Board, in a manner and format determined by the Board, within seven business days of any final action, including licence surrender or resignation, regarding a registrant or licensee by any other governmental authority in this state or another jurisdiction.

Answer the objection that it is not a pharmacy matter. The same subsection expressly reaches action against any other health care related professional registration or licence held by the registrant or licensee, so the nursing action is within it.

Take the criminal charge second. 247 CMR 10.03(1)(aa) requires report to the Board, in writing, within 30 days of any pending criminal charge or conviction, in Massachusetts or any other jurisdiction, so the duty attaches while the charge is pending rather than on any adjudication.

Notice that the two clocks are different in length, in unit and in the form the report takes: seven business days in a manner and format determined by the Board for the final action, and 30 days in writing for the criminal charge, each running from its own trigger.
worked_examples.resolution: Two separate reports were due on two separate clocks, the earlier one within seven business days of the out-of-state final action and the later one in writing within 30 days of the charge. The error the scenario invites is bundling reportable events into a single later report, with a second error behind it: reading the reporting duties as confined to pharmacy credentials and to concluded criminal cases.

worked_examples.scenario: Board investigators find that a pharmacy's compounded preparations may be contaminated. On the same day the Board President issues a Quarantine Notice prohibiting use of the medications in the pharmacy's possession, and the Board separately determines on affidavits that the supervising pharmacist is an immediate or serious threat and suspends that pharmacist's licence pending a final hearing. The pharmacy's counsel prepares one calendar entry, on the view that both actions are emergency discipline governed by a single seven-day review period.
steps: Separate the two instruments. The action against the pharmacist is a suspension prior to hearing under 247 CMR 10.07; the action against the preparations is a Quarantine Notice of the kind 247 CMR 10.08(1) permits the Board or Board President to issue.
Date the first clock. Under 247 CMR 10.07 a hearing limited to the determination of the necessity of the summary action shall be afforded the licensee within seven days of the Board's action.

Date the second clock separately. Under 247 CMR 10.08(3) a hearing limited to the determination of the necessity of the notice shall be afforded within 15 business days of the Board's or Board President's action, so the two entries do not coincide.

Fix the character of each action. The suspension is a summary action against a licence pending a final hearing on the merits; what a Cease and Desist Notice or Quarantine Notice imposes is expressly a non-disciplinary cessation or restriction pending final investigation results.
Note who may act. 247 CMR 10.07 speaks of the Board, while 247 CMR 10.08(1) and the notices in 247 CMR 10.06(8) and (9) may issue from the Board or the Board President.

Note when the notice ends. Under 247 CMR 10.08(2) its requirements remain in effect until the Board or Board President rescinds or amends them, or until the Board takes final action on any related pending complaint and issues a final decision.
worked_examples.resolution: Two hearing clocks run, seven days on the pharmacist's summary suspension and 15 business days on the Quarantine Notice, and only the first is action against a licence. The error the scenario invites is collapsing the two pre-hearing mechanisms of 247 CMR 10.07 and 10.08 into one, which also produces the further mistake of calling a notice that the regulation describes as imposing non-disciplinary restrictions a form of emergency discipline.

worked_examples.scenario: A pharmacist negotiating with the Board signs a consent agreement under which she voluntarily surrenders her personal registration for a fixed period of eighteen months, with conditions attached. Fourteen months in she regrets the bargain, and asks whether she can take the surrender to court, and what she will need to do at the end of the period to be renewed. She assumes the surrender is simply a pause and that serving out the period restores her.
steps: Establish what she signed. Under 247 CMR 10.06(6) a consent agreement is a resolution of a complaint agreed upon by the Board and the registrant which may contain conditions placed by the Board on professional conduct and practice, and which may include the voluntary suspension or surrender of a personal registration, pharmacy permit, licence or controlled substance registration; the regulation adds, of the voluntary surrender, that it may be permanent or for a fixed period of time, which is the limb she took.

Read the terms the surrender agreement must carry. It shall be in writing and signed by the registrant and the Board, shall recite the facts upon which it is based and include provisions addressing reinstatement and any conditions the Board may elect to impose, and shall be placed in her Board file as part of the permanent Board records.

Answer the question about court. The agreement shall state that the registrant realises that the surrender is an act which deprives her of all privileges of registration and is not subject to judicial review, so the waiver is a term of the document she signed rather than an argument to be made later.

Answer the question about coming back from that same document. The provisions addressing reinstatement that 247 CMR 10.06(6) requires the agreement to contain, together with any conditions the Board elected to impose in it, are where the route back is set out.

Check whether the reinstatement tiers in 247 CMR 4.02 answer it instead. 247 CMR 4.02(6) reaches an applicant for personal registration renewal whose personal registration has been revoked or has been suspended for between six months and two years, and 247 CMR 4.02(7) one whose personal registration has been revoked or suspended for more than two years. Both are written for a registration that was revoked or suspended, and neither of them names a surrender.

Keep the two sets of conditions apart. What binds her comes from the agreement, including the conditions the Board elected to impose in it; what 247 CMR 4.02(6) or (7) requires is owed by an applicant whose registration was revoked or suspended. Serving out eighteen months is not itself the route back under either.
worked_examples.resolution: The surrender is not reviewable by a court because the agreement had to say so, and serving the eighteen months does not by itself restore her: the provisions addressing reinstatement that 247 CMR 10.06(6) requires the agreement to contain, together with any conditions the Board elected to impose in it, are what govern her return. The error the scenario invites is reading a negotiated surrender as a reversible pause, and behind it the assumption that the end of the period is itself the route back to practice.

worked_examples.scenario: Three pharmacists in one chain describe their Board outcomes to each other. The first received an advisory letter after a complaint was reviewed. The second was placed on probation under a consent agreement and told to stop work at once. The third received a censure and takes comfort in it, on the view that a censure is a gentler finding than a reprimand. Each of them is wrong about something.
steps: Classify the first outcome. Under 247 CMR 10.06(2) an advisory letter is an official written document retained in the Board's files delineating the Board's concerns with the registrant's professional practice, and the regulation states that an advisory letter does not constitute formal disciplinary action.
Do not push that too far. The letter is retained in the Board's files, so it is not the same thing as no outcome at all; what it is not is formal disciplinary action.

Classify the second outcome. Under 247 CMR 10.06(4) probation constitutes disciplinary action and consists of a period of time during which the registrant may practise under conditions imposed by the Board, so probation is discipline that permits continued practice rather than a stoppage.

Identify the source of the second pharmacist's probation. 247 CMR 10.06(4) names both a formal adjudicatory hearing and a consent agreement as the routes by which probation may be imposed, so arriving there by agreement changes nothing about its character.
Classify the third outcome. Under 247 CMR 10.06(3) a reprimand constitutes formal disciplinary action and a censure is a severe reprimand, so a censure is the heavier of the two.
worked_examples.resolution: The advisory letter is not formal discipline but is retained in Board files, probation is formal discipline that expressly permits practice under conditions, and a censure is a severe reprimand rather than a lighter one. The error the scenario invites is ranking Board outcomes by how the words sound rather than by the classification 247 CMR 10.06 attaches to each of them.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: A hearing limited to the necessity of a suspension imposed prior to hearing must be afforded within ______, measured from ______.
retrieval_prompts.answer: seven days; the Board's action, under 247 CMR 10.07.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: A hearing limited to the necessity of a Cease and Desist Notice or Quarantine Notice must be afforded within ______, measured from ______.
retrieval_prompts.answer: 15 business days; the Board's or Board President's action, under 247 CMR 10.08(3).

retrieval_prompts.prompt: Two periods in this area are seven of something. Name each one, its unit, and who owes it.
retrieval_prompts.answer: Seven days is the Board's period to afford a hearing on the necessity of a summary suspension under 247 CMR 10.07. Seven business days is the registrant's or licensee's period to report discipline under 247 CMR 10.03(1)(y) and any final action by another governmental authority under 247 CMR 10.03(1)(z).

retrieval_prompts.prompt: A pending criminal charge is reported to the Board within ______ and in what form?
retrieval_prompts.answer: 30 days, in writing, under 247 CMR 10.03(1)(aa); the duty attaches while the charge is pending and does not wait for a conviction.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: True or false: an out-of-state final action against a pharmacist's nursing licence is outside the Board's reporting duties because it is not a pharmacy matter.
retrieval_prompts.answer: False. 247 CMR 10.03(1)(z) reaches any final action by any other governmental authority in this state or another jurisdiction, expressly including action against any other health care related professional registration or licence the person holds, within seven business days.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: When does a communication become a complaint within the meaning of 247 CMR 10.02?
retrieval_prompts.answer: When the Board determines, after investigation, that the communication filed with the Board or the Division of Health Professions Licensure merits further consideration or action.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: True or false: an investigative conference must be held before the Board may schedule a formal adjudicatory hearing.
retrieval_prompts.answer: False. Under 247 CMR 10.05 the Board may schedule an investigative conference or a formal adjudicatory hearing after receipt of a complaint and investigative materials, and 247 CMR 10.04 makes the conference available at any time prior to the commencement of a formal adjudicatory proceeding.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: Which document orders a registrant to appear before the Board for a formal adjudicatory hearing, and how does 247 CMR 10.02 describe it?
retrieval_prompts.answer: The Order to Show Cause, a document served by the Board upon a registrant ordering the registrant or licensee to appear before the Board for a formal adjudicatory hearing.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: Of dismissal, advisory letter, reprimand, censure, probation and revocation, which do not constitute formal disciplinary action?
retrieval_prompts.answer: Dismissal of the complaint and the advisory letter. 247 CMR 10.06(2) states that an advisory letter does not constitute formal disciplinary action, although it is an official written document retained in the Board's files.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: Which action in 247 CMR 10.06 is defined as a period of practice under conditions imposed by the Board, and does any other sanction in that regulation stop the registrant practising?
retrieval_prompts.answer: Probation, under 247 CMR 10.06(4): it constitutes disciplinary action and consists of a period of time during which the registrant or licensee may practise under conditions imposed by the Board pursuant to a formal adjudicatory hearing or consent agreement. 247 CMR 10.06(3) attaches no restriction of practice to a reprimand or a censure; the actions that take the credential away are suspension and revocation under 247 CMR 10.06(5).

retrieval_prompts.prompt: Name the four things a voluntary surrender agreement shall do under 247 CMR 10.06(6).
retrieval_prompts.answer: Be in writing and signed by the registrant or licensee and the Board; recite the facts upon which it is based and include provisions addressing reinstatement and any conditions the Board may elect to impose; state that the registrant or licensee realises the surrender deprives him or her of all privileges of registration and is not subject to judicial review; and be placed in the Board file as part of the permanent Board records.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: A consent agreement may include a voluntary suspension or a voluntary surrender. Which of the two does 247 CMR 10.06(6) say may be permanent or for a fixed period of time?
retrieval_prompts.answer: The voluntary surrender. 247 CMR 10.06(6) provides that the voluntary surrender of a personal registration, pharmacy permit, licence or controlled substance registration may be permanent or for a fixed period of time; it fixes no duration for the voluntary suspension named alongside it.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: A registration was suspended for nine months. Which subsection governs renewal, and what does it require?
retrieval_prompts.answer: 247 CMR 4.02(6), because nine months falls between six months and two years. The applicant shall take and pass the MPJE and meet all conditions as determined by the Board as a prerequisite to registration renewal; the NAPLEX is not named in that subsection.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: What is the only thing that changes between 247 CMR 4.02(6) and 247 CMR 4.02(7)?
retrieval_prompts.answer: Both require taking and passing the MPJE and meeting the conditions the Board determines. Only 4.02(7), which reaches a registration revoked or suspended for more than two years, adds that those conditions may include taking and passing the NAPLEX.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: True or false: a Cease and Desist Notice is a form of emergency discipline.
retrieval_prompts.answer: False. What the notice imposes under 247 CMR 10.08(1) is expressly a non-disciplinary cessation or restriction of pharmacy operations, or a non-disciplinary restriction on the registrant or licensee, pending final investigation results.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: How long do the requirements of a Cease and Desist Notice or Quarantine Notice remain in effect?
retrieval_prompts.answer: Until the Board or Board President rescinds or amends them, or until the Board takes final action on any related pending complaint and issues a final decision, under 247 CMR 10.08(2).

quick_review.text: A complaint under 247 CMR 10.02 is a communication filed with the Board or the Division of Health Professions Licensure which the Board determines, after investigation, merits further consideration or action.

An investigative conference is an informal discussion relating to a complaint held with the Board; an adjudicatory hearing is a formal administrative hearing under M.G.L. c. 30A and 801 CMR 1.01; an Order to Show Cause is the document served by the Board ordering the registrant to appear for that hearing.

Under 247 CMR 10.04 the Board may schedule an investigative conference at any time prior to the commencement of a formal adjudicatory proceeding, on timely notice including a general statement of the nature of the issues; under 247 CMR 10.05 it may schedule either a conference or a formal hearing after receiving the complaint and investigative materials.
247 CMR 10.06 lists the actions available to the Board, beginning with dismissal of the complaint and the advisory letter, which does not constitute formal disciplinary action.

A reprimand constitutes formal disciplinary action and a censure is a severe reprimand; probation constitutes disciplinary action and permits practice under Board-imposed conditions; suspension or revocation follows a decision and order after a formal adjudicatory hearing or the execution of a consent agreement.

Under 247 CMR 10.07 the Board may suspend or refuse to renew a licence pending a final hearing where affidavits or other documentary evidence show the licensee is an immediate or serious threat, and a hearing limited to the necessity of that action is afforded within seven days.

Under 247 CMR 10.08 the Board or Board President may issue a Cease and Desist Notice or Quarantine Notice imposing non-disciplinary cessation or restriction, with a hearing limited to its necessity within 15 business days, and the notice stands until rescinded or amended or until the Board issues a final decision on a related pending complaint.

Summary cease-and-desist and quarantine authority exists so the Board can act before a final adjudicatory hearing where a registrant or licensee, or the products prepared by one, are an immediate or serious threat to the public health, safety or welfare, and the regulation's own review procedures continue to apply.

247 CMR 10.03(1)(y) makes it a ground for discipline to fail to report, or to fail to report accurately, to the Board within seven business days and in a manner and format determined by the Board, discipline under 247 CMR 10.06 on the basis of actions listed in 247 CMR 10.03(1). 247 CMR 10.03(1)(z) runs on the same seven business days, and in the same manner and format, for any final action, including licence surrender or resignation, regarding a registrant or licensee by any other governmental authority in this state or another jurisdiction; it states the duty to report without the accuracy limb that (y) carries.
247 CMR 10.03(1)(aa) separately requires report to the Board, in writing, within 30 days of any pending criminal charge or conviction in Massachusetts or any other jurisdiction.

A consent agreement under 247 CMR 10.06(6) resolves a complaint by agreement between the Board and the registrant or licensee, may impose conditions on professional conduct and practice, and may include voluntary suspension or surrender; 247 CMR 10.06(6) attaches permanent or for a fixed period of time to the voluntary surrender, not to the voluntary suspension.

A voluntary surrender agreement is written and signed, recites the facts, addresses reinstatement and any Board conditions, states that the surrender deprives the registrant of all privileges of registration and is not subject to judicial review, and is placed in the permanent Board records.

Under 247 CMR 4.02(6) an applicant for personal registration renewal whose personal registration has been revoked or has been suspended for between six months and two years shall take and pass the MPJE and meet all conditions as determined by the Board as a prerequisite to registration renewal.

Under 247 CMR 4.02(7) a registration revoked or suspended for more than two years is renewed only on taking and passing the MPJE and meeting all other Board conditions, which may include taking and passing the NAPLEX.

decision_logic.condition: A communication about a registrant has arrived at the Board and someone asks whether a complaint is pending.
decision_logic.action: Ask whether the Board has determined, after investigation, that the communication merits further consideration or action. Until it has, the definition in 247 CMR 10.02 is not satisfied.

decision_logic.condition: The Board has a complaint and all related investigative materials in hand.
decision_logic.action: Expect a choice rather than a sequence: under 247 CMR 10.05 the Board may schedule an investigative conference or may schedule a formal adjudicatory hearing if it determines that one is required. Do not treat the conference as a mandatory first step.

decision_logic.condition: A registrant has been notified of a Board proceeding and needs to know how formal it is.
decision_logic.action: Read the notice. A notice of an investigative conference with a general statement of the nature of the issues signals the informal track under 247 CMR 10.04; an Order to Show Cause signals a formal adjudicatory hearing under M.G.L. c. 30A and 801 CMR 1.01.

decision_logic.condition: A Board outcome has to be classified as discipline or not.
decision_logic.action: Place it in 247 CMR 10.06. Dismissal and the advisory letter are not formal disciplinary action; reprimand, censure, probation, suspension and revocation are. A Cease and Desist or Quarantine Notice imposes restrictions the regulation calls non-disciplinary.

decision_logic.condition: The Board has acted before any final hearing and a review date has to be diarised.
decision_logic.action: Identify the instrument first. A suspension or refusal to renew under 247 CMR 10.07 carries a hearing on its necessity within seven days of the Board's action; a Cease and Desist or Quarantine Notice carries one within 15 business days of the Board's or Board President's action under 247 CMR 10.08(3).

decision_logic.condition: Something reportable has happened to a registrant or licensee.
decision_logic.action: Ask what kind of event it is. Discipline under 247 CMR 10.06 on the basis of actions listed in 247 CMR 10.03(1), and any final action by another governmental authority, run on seven business days in a manner and format determined by the Board; a pending criminal charge or conviction runs on 30 days and must be in writing.

decision_logic.condition: A registrant wants the matter to end without a formal adjudicatory hearing.
decision_logic.action: Look to a consent agreement under 247 CMR 10.06(6). It can carry Board conditions on professional conduct and practice, and can include a voluntary suspension or a voluntary surrender, the surrender being the one the regulation says may be permanent or for a fixed period of time; a surrender must also contain the terms 247 CMR 10.06(6) prescribes, including the statement that it is not subject to judicial review.

decision_logic.condition: A registration that was suspended or revoked is up for renewal.
decision_logic.action: Take a suspension and a revocation differently. A suspension of between six months and two years puts the applicant in 247 CMR 4.02(6) and a suspension of more than two years in 247 CMR 4.02(7); a revocation is within 4.02(6) on its terms, and within 4.02(7) once it has stood for more than two years. Either way the MPJE is required and the Board's conditions must be met; only 4.02(7) adds that those conditions may include the NAPLEX. Neither subsection is written for a suspension shorter than six months.

decision_logic.condition: A registration was never suspended or revoked but has not been renewed.
decision_logic.action: Do not use 247 CMR 4.02(6) or (7). Those subsections govern registrations that were revoked or suspended; a simple failure to renew follows a different route back, which is outside this section.

exceptions.text: The advisory letter is the carve-out inside the list of Board actions: it is an official written document retained in the Board's files, and 247 CMR 10.06(2) states that it does not constitute formal disciplinary action.

Formal discipline does not necessarily stop the registrant practising. Probation consists of a period during which the registrant or licensee may practise under conditions imposed by the Board, and 247 CMR 10.06(3) attaches no restriction of practice to a reprimand or to a censure either; what sets probation apart is that the practice is carried on under conditions the Board has imposed.

What a Cease and Desist Notice or Quarantine Notice imposes under 247 CMR 10.08(1) is expressly non-disciplinary, which is what separates it from the summary suspension in 247 CMR 10.07 even though both answer an immediate or serious threat.

A voluntary surrender agreement carries an express waiver: it shall state that the registrant or licensee realises the surrender is an act which deprives him or her of all privileges of registration and is not subject to judicial review.

The NAPLEX is not a general reinstatement requirement. It is named only in 247 CMR 4.02(7), and there only among the other conditions the Board may determine, for a registration revoked or suspended for more than two years.
Neither 247 CMR 4.02(6) nor 247 CMR 4.02(7) states a requirement for a suspension of less than six months, so neither tier should be applied to one.

timing_deadlines.event: The Board suspends or refuses to renew a licence prior to hearing under 247 CMR 10.07, on affidavits or other documentary evidence that the licensee is an immediate or serious threat to the public health, safety or welfare
timing_deadlines.timeframe: A hearing limited to the determination of the necessity of the summary action within seven days of the Board's action
timing_deadlines.consequence: The suspension or refusal to renew stands pending a final hearing on the merits, but the licensee is entitled to the necessity hearing inside seven days.

timing_deadlines.event: The Board or Board President issues a Cease and Desist Notice or Quarantine Notice under 247 CMR 10.06(8) and (9) or 247 CMR 10.08(1)
timing_deadlines.timeframe: A hearing limited to the determination of the necessity of the notice within 15 business days of the action
timing_deadlines.consequence: The registrant or licensee is entitled to a necessity hearing on a longer clock than the seven days that follows a summary suspension, and the restrictions imposed in the meantime are non-disciplinary.

timing_deadlines.event: A Cease and Desist Notice or Quarantine Notice is in force
timing_deadlines.timeframe: Until the Board or Board President rescinds or amends it, or until the Board takes final action on any related pending complaint and issues a final decision
timing_deadlines.consequence: The requirements of the notice continue to bind the registrant or licensee for that whole period under 247 CMR 10.08(2).

timing_deadlines.event: Discipline under 247 CMR 10.06 on the basis of actions listed in 247 CMR 10.03(1)
timing_deadlines.timeframe: Report to the Board within seven business days, in a manner and format determined by the Board
timing_deadlines.consequence: Failing to report, or failing to report accurately, is itself a ground for discipline under 247 CMR 10.03(1)(y).

timing_deadlines.event: Any final action, including licence surrender or resignation, regarding a registrant or licensee by any other governmental authority in this state or another jurisdiction, including action against any other health care related professional registration or licence held
timing_deadlines.timeframe: Report to the Board within seven business days, in a manner and format determined by the Board
timing_deadlines.consequence: Failing to report is a ground for discipline under 247 CMR 10.03(1)(z), and the duty is not limited to pharmacy credentials.

timing_deadlines.event: A pending criminal charge or a conviction, in Massachusetts or any other jurisdiction
timing_deadlines.timeframe: Report to the Board in writing within 30 days
timing_deadlines.consequence: Failing to report is a ground for discipline under 247 CMR 10.03(1)(aa); the duty attaches while the charge is pending and does not wait for an adjudication.

timing_deadlines.timeframe: Timely notice, given by the Board before the conference
timing_deadlines.consequence: The notice shall include a general statement of the nature of the issues to be discussed under 247 CMR 10.04.

timing_deadlines.timeframe: A period of time fixed by the Board, running from the formal adjudicatory hearing or consent agreement that imposes it
timing_deadlines.consequence: During that period the registrant or licensee may practise, but only under the conditions the Board imposes.

timing_deadlines.event: Voluntary surrender of a personal registration, pharmacy permit, licence or controlled substance registration inside a consent agreement
timing_deadlines.timeframe: Permanent, or for a fixed period of time; 247 CMR 10.06(6) says this of the voluntary surrender and states no duration for the voluntary suspension named beside it
timing_deadlines.consequence: For the duration the registrant or licensee is deprived of all privileges of registration, and the provisions addressing reinstatement that 247 CMR 10.06(6) requires the agreement to contain govern what happens next.

timing_deadlines.event: A personal registration has been revoked or has been suspended for between six months and two years
timing_deadlines.timeframe: The sanction band that selects 247 CMR 4.02(6)
timing_deadlines.consequence: The applicant shall take and pass the MPJE and meet all conditions as determined by the Board as a prerequisite to registration renewal.

timing_deadlines.event: A personal registration has been revoked or suspended for more than two years
timing_deadlines.timeframe: The sanction band that selects 247 CMR 4.02(7)
timing_deadlines.consequence: The applicant shall take and pass the MPJE and meet all other conditions as determined by the Board, which may include taking and passing the NAPLEX.

forms_records.text: The advisory letter is itself a record: an official written document retained in the Board's files delineating the Board's concerns with the registrant's or licensee's professional practice.
The Order to Show Cause is a document served by the Board upon a registrant ordering the registrant or licensee to appear before the Board for a formal adjudicatory hearing.
Notice of an investigative conference is given by the Board and shall include a general statement of the nature of the issues to be discussed.

A voluntary surrender agreement shall be in writing, be signed by the registrant or licensee and the Board, recite the facts upon which it is based, address reinstatement and any conditions the Board may elect to impose, and be placed in the registrant's or licensee's Board file as part of the permanent Board records.

Reports of discipline and of final action by another governmental authority are made to the Board in a manner and format determined by the Board; a report of a pending criminal charge or conviction is made in writing.
Suspension or revocation is recorded in a decision and order of the Board following a formal adjudicatory hearing, or in the executed consent agreement where that is the route taken.

Summary action rests on documentary material: 247 CMR 10.07 requires affidavits or other documentary evidence, and 247 CMR 10.08(1) affidavits or other evidence, before the Board or Board President acts.

role_duties.duty: Determine, after investigation, whether a communication merits further consideration or action. Having received a complaint and all related investigative materials, the Board may schedule an investigative conference, or may schedule a formal adjudicatory hearing if it determines that one is required.
Give timely notice of an investigative conference, including a general statement of the nature of the issues to be discussed.

Select an action from those available under 247 CMR 10.06. Probation under 247 CMR 10.06(4), and a suspension or revocation under 247 CMR 10.06(5), are imposed pursuant to a formal adjudicatory hearing or an executed consent agreement; that leaves untouched the separate power in 247 CMR 10.07 to suspend or refuse to renew a licence before any hearing on the merits.
Afford a hearing limited to the necessity of a summary suspension or refusal to renew within seven days of its action under 247 CMR 10.07.

Issue, and afterwards rescind or amend, a Cease and Desist Notice or Quarantine Notice where a registrant, licensee or the products prepared by one are an immediate or serious threat, and afford a hearing on the necessity of the notice within 15 business days.

Report to the Board, within seven business days and in a manner and format determined by the Board, discipline under 247 CMR 10.06 on the basis of actions listed in 247 CMR 10.03(1), and any final action by any other governmental authority in this state or another jurisdiction.
Report to the Board in writing, within 30 days, any pending criminal charge or conviction in Massachusetts or any other jurisdiction.

role_duties.role: Registrant or licensee entering a consent agreement
role_duties.duty: Sign the agreement, accept the conditions the Board places on professional conduct and practice, and, where the agreement includes voluntary surrender, sign a document stating that the surrender deprives him or her of all privileges of registration and is not subject to judicial review.

role_duties.role: Applicant for renewal after a revocation, or after a suspension of six months or more
role_duties.duty: Take and pass the MPJE and meet the conditions the Board determines under 247 CMR 4.02(6) or (7), and expect the NAPLEX to become available to the Board as a further condition only where the registration has been revoked or suspended for more than two years. Neither subsection is written for a suspension shorter than six months.

common_traps.text: Treating 247 CMR 10.00 as a fixed ladder every matter climbs. After receiving a complaint and investigative materials the Board may schedule an investigative conference or a formal adjudicatory hearing, and the conference is not a prerequisite to the hearing.

Treating any letter of grievance as a complaint. Under 247 CMR 10.02 a communication becomes a complaint only once the Board determines, after investigation, that it merits further consideration or action.

Reading an advisory letter as formal discipline because it is written and kept on file, or reading it as nothing at all because it is not discipline. It is an official written document retained in the Board's files which does not constitute formal disciplinary action.
Ranking censure below reprimand because the word sounds softer. A reprimand constitutes formal disciplinary action and a censure is a severe reprimand.
Assuming probation stops practice. Probation constitutes disciplinary action but consists of a period during which the registrant or licensee may practise under conditions imposed by the Board.

Running one clock for both pre-hearing mechanisms. A summary suspension or refusal to renew under 247 CMR 10.07 carries a seven-day necessity hearing; a Cease and Desist or Quarantine Notice carries 15 business days under 247 CMR 10.08(3).

Calling a Cease and Desist or Quarantine Notice emergency discipline. The cessation or restriction it imposes is described in the regulation as non-disciplinary, which is exactly what distinguishes it from action taken against a licence.

Confusing the two periods that are stated as seven. Seven days is the Board's clock to afford a necessity hearing; seven business days is the licensee's clock to report discipline or a final action by another governmental authority.

Waiting for a criminal case to conclude before reporting it, or bundling reportable events into one later report. 247 CMR 10.03(1)(aa) reaches a pending criminal charge and runs on 30 days, separately from the seven-business-day duties in 247 CMR 10.03(1)(y) and (z).

Reading a voluntary surrender as an informal exit that can be challenged later or simply waited out. The agreement must state that the surrender deprives the registrant of all privileges of registration and is not subject to judicial review, and it goes into the permanent Board records.

Assuming that serving out a suspension is itself the route back. Where 247 CMR 4.02(6) or (7) applies, renewal requires taking and passing the MPJE and meeting the conditions the Board determines. The trap has an edge, though: neither subsection states a requirement for a suspension shorter than six months.

Adding the NAPLEX to the shorter reinstatement tier. It is named only in 247 CMR 4.02(7), for a registration revoked or suspended for more than two years, and even there only among the conditions the Board may determine.
